reTranscriptionTest.what: The bonus graphic was read today without reference to the 13 August capture, then diffed against every figure that section states.

verifiedAgainstOurRegisters.observation: 97.7% agreement across four internal graphics and two unrelated outside registers. The GW1-3 agreement matters most: those are the cells the app will act on this week, and they now carry a third independent confirmation.
verifiedAgainstOurRegisters.aBugFoundInOurOwnChecker: The first run reported 13 further mismatches and one 'undefined'. Every one was ours: our register writes 'Spurs', 'Man City', 'Man Utd' and "Nott'm Forest" where he writes the full names, and the planner grid writes MUN where he writes MNU. A name table that does not normalise turns a parse failure into a data conflict — the same shape as the surname collisions that invented two price conflicts in the set-piece diff. Fixed before any of the numbers above were recorded.

defconLeaderboards.whatDefconIs: The +2 awarded for reaching a defensive-contribution threshold: 10 for defenders, 12 for midfielders and forwards. Our own scoring model carries the same thresholds (defconThreshold {2:10, 3:12, 4:12} in index.html).

fieldsWeAlreadyCompute.hisDefconHitRate: our dcHitLabel / _ci.dchr — the share of starts clearing the threshold
fieldsWeAlreadyCompute.hisDefconPerStart: our dcPerStartLabel / _ci.dcps — mean defensive contributions per start
fieldsWeAlreadyCompute.hisPriceBrackets: our dcByBracket, which pools everything at £6.0m and above into a top band and steps down in half-millions — the same bracketing scheme, arrived at independently. The code comment on that function reads 'Creator graphics rank DefCon leaders inside price brackets, because the real question is never who is best but who is best at the money I have left'. This thread is that graphic, and it brackets exactly that way.
fieldsWeAlreadyCompute.notADiff: These are the same QUANTITIES, not verified to be the same NUMBERS. Diffing them needs the FPL bootstrap, which this sandbox cannot reach.

opponentDefconAgainst.whatItIs: How well opposing centre-backs and central midfielders score DEFCON when playing AGAINST each club — i.e. which fixtures feed a DEFCON pick.
opponentDefconAgainst.coverage: 17 clubs, not 20. Coventry, Ipswich and Hull are absent because they were not in the division last season, which is the same reason the £4m defenders above are all Championship rows.
opponentDefconAgainst.hisOwnCaveat: 'A good number of teams have changed managers in the summer' — he marks eleven of the seventeen CB rows and eight of the CM rows with an asterisk. That is the author telling you his own table's shelf life, and it should be quoted whenever the table is.

theDefectThisSurfacedInOurApp.found: 2026-08-16, while checking whether our DEFCON fields matched his
theDefectThisSurfacedInOurApp.what: dcHitRate() always returns a number. For a defender with no Premier League history there is no _ci record (it is keyed on FPL element ids) and no per-90, so the logistic fell through to ~0% — rendered in the scouting table's 'DC hit%' column and in the DefCon lens as though it were a measurement.
theDefectThisSurfacedInOurApp.whyItMatters: ~0% reads as 'this player never clears the threshold'. It actually meant 'we have never seen him play here'. A defender with 2,000 minutes and genuinely no defensive returns rendered identically, and those are not the same claim.
theDefectThisSurfacedInOurApp.howThisThreadFoundIt: His entire cheapest defensive bracket (£4m) is nine Championship players, and his headline recommendation was to gamble on Vuskovic (Bundesliga), Muharemovic (Serie A) and Jacquet (Ligue 1). Every one of those twelve is a player our tool rated ~0%. The instrument was most confident exactly where it knew least, and the cheapest bracket is where enablers come from, so the blind spot sat on the most-used part of the table.
theDefectThisSurfacedInOurApp.fixed: dcHasBasis() now gates the label: no Premier League minutes at all gives '—' rather than a percentage, and the column sorts those with the unrateable rows instead of below the worst rated defender. The floor is any real minutes rather than a threshold, so a genuine ~0% from a real season survives — that one is a true finding.
theDefectThisSurfacedInOurApp.alreadySafe: dcByBracket already excluded zero-minute players from the budget ladder, and the player card was already gated on _ci. This closed the two places that were not.
theDefectThisSurfacedInOurApp.testedBy: dev/test-core.mjs, section 'dcHitLabel: "never clears it" and "never seen him" are different claims' — seven assertions including the regression that the two cases must not render identically.
theDefectThisSurfacedInOurApp.theRecurringShape: This is the fourth time in a fortnight the same failure has been recorded: a check reporting its own coverage as a finding about the world. The others were the silent MID fallback in provider.js, gradeEfl unable to tell 'checked' from 'not deployed', and the briefing parser's last club block swallowing three sections. When a check finds nothing, the first question is whether it could have found anything.

flagsRaisedNotResolved.why: We hold our own dchr and dcps. They have NOT been diffed against his, because that needs the FPL bootstrap. Until they are, agreement between his figures and ours is assumed, not shown — and this file must not be read as confirming our numbers.

gradeableAfterTheSeasonStarts: Whether the £5m defensive bracket is the 'sweet spot' he calls it, measured as points per million against the £4.5m and £5.5m brackets.

Whether the three foreign-league gambles (Vuskovic, Muharemovic, Jacquet) reproduce their DEFCON rates in the Premier League — the explicit bet of the thread, and the one our model structurally cannot make.
Whether Man United's GW1-3 and Liverpool's GW2-4 runs, which he ranks 2nd and 4th best in the whole first half of the season, actually return above average.

The custom FDR itself: bookmaker odds plus last season's home/away record, against outcomes. We hold two other fixture-difficulty scales — our own four-band labels and the fplrotationplanner grid — so round-by-round this is a three-way calibration set rather than a single opinion.
The Sunderland GW4 venue, which settles outright the moment the fixtures endpoint is read.
whatThisChangesInOurDocuments: The briefing price table gains three settled rows (Saka, Ndiaye, Garner), taking the outside table to 7 right from 7 and ours to 0.
Nothing else. No pick, no rating and no model weight is changed by this file. It is a benchmark to be graded, not an input.
